# SAF-T test schema

`saft-2.00-tax-extract.xsd` is NOT the official OECD SAF-T 2.0 schema. It is a hand-written subset that keeps the OECD namespace (`urn:OECD:StandardAuditFile-Tax:2.00`), the `AuditFile` root, the `Header` fields the exporter fills (AuditFileVersion, AuditFileCountry, AuditFileDateCreated, Software*, Company, DefaultCurrencyCode, SelectionCriteria) and a `MasterFiles/TaxTable` of per-code period totals, optional `Customers` and `Suppliers`, and optional `GeneralLedgerEntries` (a field subset, not the full OECD content model).

Why: the OECD publishes the full XSD on oecd.org, which answered HTTP 403 to every automated download when this was built, and no verbatim mirror of the 2.0 schema could be found. Nothing here was invented to look official: the file says what it is.

To close AC4 fully: download the official 2.0 XSD from the OECD guidance page (https://www.oecd.org/tax/forum-on-tax-administration/publications-and-products/guidance-for-the-standard-audit-file-tax-version-2-0.htm), commit it verbatim next to this file with its sha256 and retrieval date recorded here, point `TestExport_ValidatesAgainstTheSchema` at it, then diff it against this subset. Customers, Suppliers and GeneralLedgerEntries are in the subset and are also checked in Go by `internal/saft/check.go` (required fields, unique ids, positive debit/credit choice, balanced transactions, control totals, party references).

Strict-subset rule: the file starts with a comment saying it must accept nothing the official schema would reject in shape. Where this subset models an element it follows the official 2.00 structure as far as it is known here (AmountStructure with `Amount` plus optional `CurrencyCode`, `CurrencyAmount`, `ExchangeRate`; `GeneralLedgerAccounts/Account` with AccountID, AccountDescription, AccountType and a debit/credit choice for opening and closing balance; Transaction with TransactionID, Period, PeriodYear, TransactionDate, Description, SystemEntryDate, GLPostingDate and at least two Lines). The element order and the required elements were written from memory of the specification, not from the official file, so compare them when the official XSD is fetched. Not modelled: the rest of the Header (company address, tax accounting basis, tax entity), the other MasterFiles tables, SourceDocuments, and the optional Transaction, Line and Account elements beyond those above.
